title: 6 Best Asphalt Driveway Sealers in 2026: Picks by Surface Wear
metaDescription: Latex-ite Airport Grade tops 6 asphalt driveway sealers for most faded blacktop, with coats that last 2-3 years. Pails ranked by filler, finish and weather.
h1: The 6 Best Asphalt Driveway Sealers in 2026
keywords: best asphalt driveway sealer and crack filler
intro:
The best asphalt driveway sealer for most homeowners is Latex-ite Airport Grade, a filled, polymer-modified emulsion that covers moderate wear, rinses off tools with water and sits on shelves almost everywhere. Whatever pail you buy, plan on the coat lasting two to three years, no matter what number is printed on the lid.

The right pick depends on what your blacktop looks like today. A smooth, sound driveway wants a different product than a gray, open-textured one, and a driveway sealed two summers ago may only need a thin refresh. Below you will find six products ranked for those situations, followed by the questions people ask most: which type to buy, how many pails, how to prep, and when the weather is right.
quickAnswer: Buy Latex-ite Airport Grade for a typical faded asphalt driveway. Choose Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 when the surface is smooth and the finish matters, Jetcoat Premium for rough, weathered blacktop, and Henry or Gardner for a cheap refresh on a driveway sealed recently. Fill cracks wider than about 1/8 inch with Latex-ite Pli-Stix before any sealer goes down.

sections.heading: Best Asphalt Driveway Sealer: The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Pick | Best for | Key spec |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latex-ite Airport Grade | Most faded driveways | Polymer-modified emulsion with filler |
| Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 | Best finish on smooth asphalt | Filler plus rubberized polymer |
| Jetcoat Premium | Rough, weathered blacktop | Heavy-bodied filled emulsion |
| Henry Asphalt Driveway Filler & Sealer | Lowest cost on a sound drive | Water-based emulsion with filler |
| Gardner Blacktop Driveway Sealer | Thin maintenance coats | Basic emulsion, little or no filler |
| Latex-ite Pli-Stix | Crack prep before sealing | Rubberized rope filler, torch-applied |

Under the brand names, nearly every retail asphalt sealer is the same basic recipe: refined asphalt suspended in water with clay, plus varying amounts of mineral filler, sand and polymer. What separates one pail from another is how much solid material it carries, whether it has filler for rough surfaces, and how forgiving it is of marginal weather.

So match the product to the surface. Filled, polymer-modified pails earn their price on aging driveways; thin, cheap pails make sense only on blacktop that is already tight and dark. If your driveway is concrete, none of these belong on it; see the [best concrete driveway sealer picks](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) instead.

sections.heading: The 6 Best Asphalt Driveway Sealers in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
The ranking draws on manufacturer data sheets and pail labels (formula, cure times, temperature limits), how easy each product is to buy in matching batches, and patterns in owner reports about how a coat holds up through its first winter. Coverage and solids vary by batch and region, so confirm them on the pail you actually pick up.

### Best Overall: Latex-ite Airport Grade

Latex-ite has been a homeowner driveway brand for decades, and Airport Grade is the top of its retail range. It is a water-based asphalt emulsion with mineral filler and polymer added, which gives it noticeably more body than an entry-level pail. That body matters on a driveway that has started to gray and roughen: the filler packs into the open texture instead of soaking away, so the surface comes out more even after two coats. The label calls for 50°F and rising, with dry weather afterward, which is standard for the category. Owners commonly report that the black holds well through the first year and that the cured film resists tire scuffs better than budget products. The trade-offs are cost per pail and effort. The filler settles hard in storage, so mix every pail with a drill paddle, and expect an oxidized surface to use more than the coverage line suggests.

**Pros:** Filler bridges hairline cracks and evens out texture; water cleanup and mild odor; sold widely, so matching pails is easy; deep, uniform black that hides patches.

**Cons:** Costs more per pail than basic emulsions; heavy filler takes real mixing; coverage drops on very porous blacktop.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Latex-ite+Airport+Grade+driveway+sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Premium Finish: Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000

Black Jack is the brand stacked near the front doors of many home centers, and Drive-Maxx 1000 is its flagship. It is a water-based emulsion with filler and a rubberized polymer intended to make the film tougher and more flexible, and it cures to one of the darkest, most even blacks you can buy in a retail pail. That finish is why people choose it before listing a house or simply because the driveway is the first thing visitors see. On a smooth, sound surface, the look is worth the premium. On rough, gray asphalt the advantage narrows, because any filled sealer will soak in on the first coat and need a second to even out. Read the large number on the front as a product tier, not a promise of years between coats. Owners most often praise how evenly it spreads under a squeegee; the most common complaint is price.

**Pros:** Very dark, uniform finish; filler and rubberized polymer for a tougher film; water-based cleanup; easy to find in most regions.

**Cons:** Top-of-range price; finish advantage shrinks on rough, oxidized blacktop.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Black+Jack+Drive-Maxx+1000&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Rough Surfaces: Jetcoat Premium

Jetcoat Premium is a heavy-bodied filled emulsion aimed at driveways that have gone several seasons without care. When the fine material between the stones has washed out, a thin sealer simply disappears into the gaps. A thicker filled product sits higher, closes part of that texture and leaves a more uniform surface. Owners commonly report that it covers weathered driveways better than budget pails and that one coat is enough to freshen a surface that only needed a little help. The heavier body takes more effort to push with a brush, and like every pail here, the long-life wording on the front is a tier name rather than a service life. Check the formula on the exact pail you buy, since product lines differ by region and you want to know whether you are applying an asphalt emulsion. For an aging driveway on a moderate budget, it is a sensible middle choice.

**Pros:** Thick, filled formula for open-textured asphalt; good value per pail versus flagship lines; easy to buy online and in hardware stores; even matte black.

**Cons:** Long-life label wording is not a guarantee; harder to spread with a brush.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jetcoat+Premium+driveway+sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Budget: Henry Asphalt Driveway Filler & Sealer

Henry has made asphalt roof and paving coatings for a long time, and its driveway filler-sealer is the low-cost workhorse here. It is a water-based emulsion with enough filler for hairline cracks and light wear, and it moves quickly under a squeegee. Owners describe it as a good maintenance coat for driveways sealed in the past few years that just need their color and water resistance renewed. It is less convincing on badly oxidized surfaces, where the first coat soaks in and a second is needed to look even. That second coat is the real cost question: two coats of a budget pail can approach the cost of one and a half coats of a premium one, so price the whole job rather than a single pail. The film is thinner than flagship tiers, so plan to recoat at the short end of the two-to-three-year cycle.

**Pros:** Low price per pail keeps big jobs affordable; filler handles hairline cracks; low odor and water cleanup; long-standing coatings brand.

**Cons:** Thinner film, so recoat sooner; holds less color depth after a year of sun.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Henry+asphalt+driveway+filler+sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Maintenance Coats: Gardner Blacktop Driveway Sealer

Gardner shares a corporate family with Black Jack and sells a basic blacktop sealer with a narrow but real job. On a driveway that is smooth, structurally sound and sealed within the last few years, a thin coat brings back the black color and renews water resistance without building up a thick layer. That restraint is useful, because stacking heavy coats year after year is a common cause of cracking and flaking. What Gardner cannot do is fill texture or bridge cracks. On gray, open blacktop it soaks in, looks blotchy and needs extra coats, which erases the price advantage. Owners report that it goes on fast and looks sharp at first, then fades sooner than filled products. Use it between full sealing cycles on the right driveway and it is good value; use it to rescue a worn-out one and it will disappoint.

**Pros:** Cheap and easy to find; thin enough to spread quickly; low-odor, water-based; handy for touch-ups.

**Cons:** Little or no filler, so no help on rough or cracked asphalt; wears out sooner than filled products.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Gardner+blacktop+driveway+sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Prep Companion: Latex-ite Pli-Stix

Pli-Stix is not a sealer, but it may do more for the life of your next coat than any pail on this list. Sealer usually fails first at cracks, where water slips under the film and freeze-thaw cycles pry it loose. Pli-Stix is a rubberized rope filler: you press a length into a clean, dry crack and melt it with a propane torch until it flows and grips the crack walls. Once it cools it stays flexible as the pavement moves, and sealer can be squeegeed right over it. Owners commonly report that it survives winter better than pourable fillers in medium cracks, and that the main skill is keeping the flame moving. Keep a hose nearby, since dry grass and leaves catch quickly. It is made for small and medium cracks; wide gaps, potholes and sunken areas need cold patch or a paving contractor.

**Pros:** Stays flexible through temperature swings; no mixing; sealer goes straight over it once cool; outlasts sealer alone in cracks.

**Cons:** Requires a torch and care around dry vegetation; not for wide gaps or potholes.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Latex-ite+Pli-Stix+crack+filler&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: Which Asphalt Driveway Sealer Is Right for Your Driveway?
sections.body:
The condition of the blacktop picks the product more reliably than the brand does. Walk the driveway on a dry day, pour a cup of water on the busiest spot, and match what you see to one of the cases below.

### Smooth, sound and only slightly faded

Choose Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 if looks come first, or Latex-ite Airport Grade for the best balance of durability and price. Both leave a deep, even black on a tight surface without much prep beyond cleaning.

### Gray, rough and soaking up water

Go with a filled product such as Jetcoat Premium or Latex-ite Airport Grade, and brush the first coat in to push material into the texture. A surface like this drinks more than the label suggests, so buy extra. Close cracks with Pli-Stix or a pourable filler first.

### Sealed in the last two or three years

Henry or Gardner is enough. A thin coat renews the color and water resistance without adding a thick layer that will crack later. Before buying anything, confirm the driveway actually needs it: if water still beads, wait a year.

### Very long or shared driveways

Past roughly 1,500 square feet, get a contractor quote before you buy a pile of pails. Crews buy bulk material and often land close to the cost of premium retail sealer while saving you two days of hauling and squeegeeing. Our guide on [how much it costs to seal a driveway](/how-much-does-it-cost-to-seal-a-driveway/) shows how DIY and contractor numbers compare by size.

sections.heading: What Are the Main Types of Asphalt Sealer?
sections.body:
Almost every driveway sealer you will find falls into one of four families. The family tells you more about how a pail will behave than the brand or the years on the lid.

| Type | Base | Best for | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Asphalt emulsion | Asphalt, clay, water, emulsifier | Most home driveways | Needs warm, dry weather to cure |
| Polymer-modified emulsion | Emulsion plus latex or rubber | Higher traffic, scuff resistance | Higher price per pail |
| Coal tar emulsion | Refined coal tar pitch, water, clay | Fuel and oil resistance | Restricted in some states and cities; odor and skin irritation |
| Oil-based (cutback) | Asphalt dissolved in solvent | Very dry, old asphalt | Fumes, VOC limits, slow cure |

### Why emulsions dominate the shelf

Asphalt emulsions are water-based, wash off tools with a hose until they cure, smell mild, and use the same kind of binder the driveway is made from. Quality varies a lot within the family. The cheapest pails are thin and lose color first; better ones add filler for body and polymer for flexibility.

### Is an oil based driveway sealer better?

Rarely, for a home driveway. Oil-based sealers soak into very dry asphalt rather than sitting on it, which some owners like on old surfaces, but they smell strongly, cure slowly and run into volatile organic compound limits in some states. A good filled emulsion is the simpler choice for most people.

### How to tell which chemistry is in the pail

Read the cleanup directions. Water cleanup means an emulsion; mineral spirits means a solvent product. Warnings about sun sensitivity, skin contact or local restrictions point to coal tar. If the label does not say plainly, choose a pail that does.

sections.heading: Is Coal Tar Sealer Better Than Asphalt Emulsion?
sections.body:
For a home driveway, no. Coal tar resists gasoline and motor oil better than asphalt-based sealers, which is why it became the standard on gas station aprons and commercial lots. On a residential driveway that sees the occasional drip from a parked car, that edge is small, and the downsides are large.

### The health and environmental concern

Coal tar sealers contain high levels of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), a group of compounds that includes known and probable carcinogens. U.S. Geological Survey research has reported PAH levels in coal tar sealcoat roughly a thousand times higher than in asphalt-based sealcoat, and has linked coal tar sealed pavement to raised PAH levels in nearby house dust and stream sediment as the coating wears off.

### Where it is restricted

Washington and Minnesota restrict coal tar sealers statewide, and many cities and counties elsewhere ban their sale or use. Rules change over time, so check your state and local regulations before buying anything labeled coal tar or refined tar. Even where it is legal, it smells strongly and can irritate skin and eyes during application, especially in sun.

### What to use instead

A quality asphalt emulsion gives comparable everyday protection on a driveway. Treat known drip spots with an oil spot primer before sealing, and clean up fresh drips promptly. If a contractor proposes a coal tar product, ask for an asphalt-based alternative. For a broader look at whether sealing is worth doing at all, see [should asphalt driveways be sealed](/sealing-asphalt-driveway-pros-and-cons/).

sections.heading: Does the Number of Years on the Pail Mean Anything?
sections.body:
Not as a lifespan. The big three, six, eight or ten printed on many pails is best read as the product's position in the brand's lineup. Paving trade groups generally advise resealing residential driveways every two to three years regardless of the label.

### What actually decides how long a coat lasts

Traffic, sun, snowplows and prep. A coat on a busy driveway in full afternoon sun that gets plowed all winter wears faster than one on a shaded drive that sees one car on weekends. A thin first coat over dust wears fastest of all.

### The label specs that matter

Turn the pail around. The useful numbers are coverage per pail, minimum application temperature, wait time before foot and vehicle traffic, and whether the formula includes filler or sand. Filled sealers usually say so with words like filler-sealer or for rough surfaces. A thin maintenance sealer tends to list higher coverage, because there is less solid material to spread.

### What a sealer warranty covers

Where a written guarantee exists, it typically covers product defects only, with a refund or replacement product as the remedy, not your labor or a contractor bill. Most require that you followed the application directions, including temperature and cure time. Keep the receipt and a photo of the batch code if it matters to you, but never choose a pail for its warranty.

sections.heading: How Many Pails of Driveway Sealer Do You Need?
sections.body:
Divide the driveway area by the label coverage, double it for two coats, and add one pail as a cushion. A 600-square-foot driveway with a sealer rated at 300 square feet per pail needs two pails per coat, four for the job, and a fifth for safety.

### Measuring the driveway

Measure in feet, multiply length by width for each rectangular section, and add the sections. Most two-car driveways run 400 to 800 square feet. A long rural drive can exceed 2,000 square feet, which is where contractor pricing starts to look attractive.

### Typical planning numbers

| Item | Typical figure |
| --- | --- |
| Label coverage per pail | About 250 to 400 sq ft |
| Coats | Two thin coats |
| Minimum temperature | 50°F and rising |
| Wait before driving | 24 to 48 hours |

### Why the label coverage runs optimistic

Coverage figures assume fairly smooth, sound asphalt. On a first coat over oxidized, porous blacktop, owners commonly find they use a quarter to a third more. A driveway that uses less than the label is rare, so always round up.

### Buy every pail at once

Color can shift slightly between batches, so buy the whole job together and match batch codes when you can. An unopened spare keeps until next season if stored above freezing. Do not use a pail that froze over winter: a broken emulsion shows up as lumps that will not remix.

sections.heading: How Do You Prep and Apply Asphalt Driveway Sealer?
sections.body:
Clean it, treat oil, fill cracks, let it dry, then lay two thin coats. Most early peeling traces back to a dirty or damp surface, so give prep as much time as the coating itself.

### Step 1: Edge and clean

Trim grass back from the edges so sealer reaches the true pavement edge. Sweep hard with a stiff push broom, blow off debris and wash the surface. A pressure washer helps on mossy or grimy blacktop; keep the tip moving and go easy on soft, raveling areas. If moss has taken hold, clear it first using our guide to [removing moss from an asphalt driveway](/how-to-remove-moss-from-asphalt-driveway/).

### Step 2: Treat oil spots

Sealer will not bond over oil, and oil can bleed up through a new coat. Scrub stains with a driveway degreaser, rinse, and brush on an oil spot primer. Our guide to [removing oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/) covers products that will not soften asphalt.

### Step 3: Fill cracks and let it dry

Filled sealer bridges hairline cracks, but anything wider than about 1/8 inch needs a dedicated filler and time to cure. Then give the surface at least a full sunny day to dry.

### Squeegee or brush?

Use a squeegee on reasonably smooth asphalt and a stiff brush on rough, porous surfaces. Many owners brush the first coat in and squeegee the second. Stir each pail thoroughly with a drill paddle, cut in the edges with a brush, tape off concrete and siding (asphalt sealer stains concrete permanently), and work from the garage toward the street.

### Why two thin coats beat one thick coat

A heavy coat skins over on top while the layer below stays soft. It cures slowly, picks up tire marks and cracks as it shrinks. Let the first coat dry to the touch, usually a few hours on a warm, sunny day, then apply the second at right angles.

sections.heading: What Temperature and Weather Do You Need to Seal Asphalt?
sections.body:
Most asphalt sealer labels call for air and pavement at 50°F or warmer and rising, staying above that through the following night, with a dry forecast for at least a day after you finish. A few premium products ask for 55°F. Water-based sealers cure by evaporation, so weather controls the whole job.

### The sealing season

Across most of the country, late spring through early fall works. Very hot pavement causes its own problems, since sealer can flash-dry on top before it bonds. On scorching days, start early in the morning or mist the surface lightly with a hose if the label allows it. Our guide to the [minimum temperature for sealing a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/) breaks down the air, pavement and overnight readings that decide the day.

### What happens if it rains

Rain is the most common way a fresh coat gets ruined. A shower in the first few hours can wash uncured sealer into the street and leave a thin, streaky surface. Check the hourly forecast, not just the daily high.

### When can you drive on it?

Foot traffic is usually fine after several hours. Most labels want 24 to 48 hours before cars, longer in cool or humid weather. For the first week, avoid turning the steering wheel while the car is stopped; that is what scuffs a soft coat.

### New blacktop needs to wait

Fresh asphalt needs about six months to a year for its oils to cure before sealer bonds well. A new driveway that looks gray is often just dusty. See [when to seal a new asphalt driveway](/when-should-you-seal-a-new-asphalt-driveway/) for the signs it is ready.

mistakes.title: Sealing new asphalt too soon
mistakes.body: Fresh blacktop is still releasing oils and stays softer than it will be in a year. Sealer applied early can trap those oils, bond poorly and scuff under tires. Wait at least six months, ideally a full year, unless your paving contractor gave a specific shorter interval for their mix.

mistakes.title: Resealing every year out of habit
mistakes.body: Extra coats do not add protection. Each one adds thickness, and a heavy buildup eventually cracks and flakes, taking newer layers with it. Most home driveways need a coat every two to three years. If water still beads and the surface is still dark, skip a year.

mistakes.title: Pouring without stirring
mistakes.body: Filler and sand pack down hard in storage. Skip the mixing and the first half of the driveway gets watery sealer while the second gets sludge, and the finish shows both. Run a drill paddle through every pail until the color and texture match from top to bottom.

mistakes.title: Laying one thick coat to save time
mistakes.body: A heavy coat forms a skin while the layer beneath stays soft, so it cures slowly, marks under tires and cracks as it shrinks. Two thin coats use about the same material and produce a tougher, more even film. The cost is an extra afternoon, not extra sealer.

mistakes.title: Ignoring the hourly forecast
mistakes.body: Water-based sealer needs warm, dry hours to cure. A cold night or a thunderstorm in the first 24 hours can leave the coat soft, streaky or washed into the gutter. Check the hourly forecast through the next morning and wait for several dry days above the label minimum.

faqs.q: What is the best asphalt driveway sealer?
faqs.a: For most faded driveways, Latex-ite Airport Grade is the safest pick. It is a filled, polymer-modified emulsion with enough body to cover moderate wear, it cleans up with water, and it is stocked widely enough to buy matching pails. Choose Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 instead when the blacktop is smooth and you want the darkest, most even finish.

faqs.q: What is the best driveway sealer according to Consumer Reports?
faqs.a: This guide does not reproduce or rely on Consumer Reports ratings, which sit behind their paywall. The ranking here comes from manufacturer data sheets, pail labels, availability and owner reports. On that basis, Latex-ite Airport Grade suits most faded asphalt driveways, Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 gives the best finish on smooth blacktop, and Henry is the strongest budget pick.

faqs.q: How long does asphalt driveway sealer last?
faqs.a: Plan on two to three years on most home driveways, whatever the pail claims. Heavy traffic, full sun, snowplows and a thin first coat shorten that, while shade, light traffic and two careful coats stretch it. Use a water test each spring: when water soaks in instead of beading, the driveway is ready for another coat.

faqs.q: What is the best asphalt driveway sealer and crack filler?
faqs.a: Use a filled sealer for hairline cracks and a separate filler for anything wider. Latex-ite Airport Grade bridges fine cracks on its own. For cracks wider than about 1/8 inch, Latex-ite Pli-Stix is a rubberized rope filler melted in with a propane torch; it stays flexible through winter, and sealer can go straight over it once cool.

faqs.q: Is oil based driveway sealer better than water based?
faqs.a: Not for most home driveways. Oil-based sealers penetrate very dry asphalt, but they smell strongly, cure slowly and face VOC limits in some states. Water-based asphalt emulsions clean up with a hose, carry little odor and protect a sound driveway well. Polymer-modified emulsions add scuff resistance for higher-traffic drives.

faqs.q: Can you use asphalt sealer on a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: No. Asphalt sealer bonds poorly to concrete, peels, tracks black into the house and permanently stains any concrete it touches. Tape off walkways and garage aprons when you seal blacktop. A concrete driveway needs a penetrating silane-siloxane or a concrete-rated acrylic; our concrete driveway sealer roundup covers those products.

faqs.q: How long after sealing can you drive on a driveway?
faqs.a: Most labels say 24 to 48 hours before cars, and longer when the weather is cool or humid. Walking is usually fine after a few hours once the surface is dry to the touch. For the first week, roll forward slightly before turning the wheel, because twisting tires on a soft coat leaves scuff marks.

bottomLine: Latex-ite Airport Grade is the asphalt driveway sealer to buy for most driveways: filled, polymer-modified, easy to apply and sold nearly everywhere. Pay more for Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 when the blacktop is smooth and the finish matters, choose Jetcoat Premium for rough surfaces, and save with Henry or Gardner on a driveway sealed recently. Prep matters more than the brand: clean thoroughly, fill cracks with something like Pli-Stix, lay two thin coats in warm, dry weather, keep cars off for two days, and repeat every two to three years rather than every spring.
